deepdive.sec: Civil Infrastructure / Construction EPC (Metro · Sports · Water · Green Buildings)

bull_bear.body:
- **Warrants + preferential** are the primary funding lever (also the reason finance cost fell); MD subscribing personally = skin-in-the-game (but adds dilution on top of the FY26 bonus + preferential that tripled share capital).
- Promoter holding **~63–67%** (mgmt gave a range).
- Working-capital discipline: matching payables cycle (~90 days) to receivables; **~85–87% of year-end receivables collected within ~30–45 days** post year-end.
- No dividend/buyback commentary. Reinvestment-for-growth phase.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **Steep scale-up execution:** ~Rs 240 cr FY26 → Rs 600 cr (FY27) → Rs 900 cr (FY28) is a ~2.5x jump in two years; mgmt says teams, plant & machinery and major procurement are already in place ("ahead of time," "no risk currently") — credibility check pending.
- **Working-capital intensity / government receivables:** trade receivables rose sharply (chat-box flagged a >10x jump — mgmt clarified the figure is in **lakhs not crores**, ~Rs 80–87 cr, ~80% collected within 30 days); classic government-EPC payment-cycle risk.
- **Funding dependence on warrants/preferential:** if warrant subscription or milestone collections slip, the WC bridge tightens; further dilution possible.
- **Aligarh JV is very long-dated** (78–96 months) — optionality, not near-term value.
- **Nascent verticals (data-centre cooling, tunnel ventilation) have no orders yet** — narrative optionality until Q2 update.
- **Margin-mix risk** as revenue scales via large metro contracts (typically lower-margin than niche work).
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body:
- Promotional, confident tone; several answers were vague or garbled ("easily possible," "H1 vs H2 will be great"), and the FY-EBITDA rupee figure looks misstated — precision on numbers is a watch-item.
- Positives: **MD personally subscribed to warrants** (alignment); proactively **clarified Jiya Eco is not a Univastu acquisition**; explained the conservative <25%-completion revenue-recognition policy; addressed receivables lakhs-vs-crores confusion.
- Declined to comment on share price ("dull movement" question) — appropriately.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- **Class 1A unlimited licence is the structural edge** — lets Univastu bid large government tenders on its own merit without sharing margin with JV partners; underpins the solo-bid, in-house-execution margin story.
- **The 600/900 cr guide is more execution- than order-dependent** — ~Rs 1,500 cr of the existing backlog is already slated for FY28, and mgmt models **zero revenue from new FY27 wins**, so new orders (target ≥Rs 1,000 cr) are pure upside.
- **Q4 margin dip is mechanical, not structural** — the <25%-completion no-profit POC policy means a wave of new-site mobilization front-loads cost and defers profit; normalization is a policy artifact, verifiable next quarter.
- **Niche-vertical strategy (Metro-BMS, tunnel ventilation, Myrtha pools, DC cooling) is explicitly a margin-defence play** against commoditized civil-EPC competition — but three of these are still pre-order.
- Dilution is the quiet cost of the growth: FY26 bonus + preferential tripled share capital, and more warrants are being issued to fund the scale-up.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

business.body:
- **Metro (core growth):** civil + in-house Metro-BMS; Pune Metro executed via T&T and ANSH JVs (hit qualification bars without locking 100% own capital).
- **Sports infrastructure:** Myrtha Pools (Italy) tie-up — Olympic official partner; described as a near-"monopoly" edge for premium sports/pool bids; low own-overhead.
- **Net-zero / green buildings:** via **Bootes Infra LLP**, expanding North-India footprint at **16–17% operating margins**.
- **Niche verticals:** Metro-BMS, tunnel ventilation, data-centre works — "lower competition → better margins than regular civil work."
- **In-house model:** firefighting, all electrical, and works done in-house; purchases direct from OEMs — cited as the margin/rate advantage vs large EPC players who sub-contract.
- Revenue recognition: **percentage-of-completion**, conservative — **no profit margin recognized below 25% project completion** (only cost = revenue until then, then full POC).

latest_quarter.body:
- **Raw-material / war-driven inflation** flagged by analysts — mgmt says **all contracts include escalation clauses**, so inflation is passed through and "will not hurt margins."
- Q4 EBITDA margin (13.94%) below the FY 17.10% level because multiple large new sites were mobilized simultaneously (front-loaded setup costs + conservative <25%-completion no-profit policy) — mgmt expects normalization.
- In-house execution (electrical, firefighting, BMS) vs peers' sub-contracting is the cited margin lever; OEM-direct purchasing keeps bid rates competitive.
- Finance cost down 6.59% (FY) despite balance-sheet growth — driven by equity/warrant inflow, not debt refinancing.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

latest_quarter.body:
- **Q4 FY26 & FY26 (this):** Revenue Rs 243.35 cr FY26 (+42.16%); Q4 Rs 109.44 cr (+174% YoY). PAT Rs 25.69 cr (+65%+); FY EPS 6.48. EBITDA margin 17.10% FY / 13.94% Q4. Order book Rs 1,854 cr (~2x book-to-bill) → ~Rs 2,000 cr+ post-year-end (IRCON Rs 100 cr + Aligarh). Q4 inflow Rs 1,317 cr (MMRDA ML-6, L&T ML-4). Guide: Rs 600 cr FY27 / Rs 900 cr FY28, 17–18% EBITDA, 10–11% PAT; ≥Rs 1,000 cr new-order target FY27 (bidding from end-Q2). Warrants (~Rs 14 cr July inflow, MD subscribed) funding scale-up; finance cost −6.59%; D/E ~0.3; positive OCF. New verticals: DC liquid cooling + tunnel ventilation (pre-order); Aligarh land-JV (49%, ~Rs 250 cr rev / 20% EBITDA, 78–96 months). Jiya Eco NOT acquired by Univastu.
- _Next Q (Q1/H1 FY27) → check: Rs 600 cr FY27 trajectory & quarterly run-rate; ≥Rs 1,000 cr new-order wins (bidding starts end-Q2); EBITDA back toward 17–18% as new sites cross 25% completion; data-centre cooling order (Q2 update promised); tunnel-ventilation first order (~6 months); warrant inflow received; receivables/OCF discipline held._

outlook.body:
- **Revenue:** FY27 **~Rs 600 cr**; FY28 **~Rs 900 cr**; framed as ">2x revenue CAGR in the current year." ~Rs 1,500 cr of the existing order book is slated for execution by FY28.
- **New order target (FY27):** **minimum Rs 1,000 cr of new orders/pipeline** this financial year. **Not bidding in Q1**; will bid from end of Q2. Explicitly **no revenue inflow modelled from the new pipeline this FY** (design-build lag — revenue starts only after design/build phase). New wins would be **additive** to the 600/900 cr guide.
- **Margins:** PAT margin held at **10–11%**; **EBITDA 17–18%** "easily" for FY27 and FY28. All contracts carry **price-escalation clauses**, so raw-material/war-driven inflation is passed through.
- **Cash flow:** operating cash flow turned positive in FY26; **positive OCF expected again in FY27**. D/E ~0.3 to stay "within limits."
- **Capex/new segments:** tunnel ventilation first order ≥6 months out; data-centre (liquid-to-liquid cooling) order visibility deferred to the Q2 call; Aligarh JV long-dated (see §8).
outlook.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)

outlook.body:
- **Rs 1,854 cr** closing order book (Mar-26), spread across **5 states** (Maharashtra, UP, Gujarat, Haryana + one more) — deliberately de-concentrated by geography.
- **Q4 fresh orders Rs 1,317 cr** — marquee Tier-1 clients: **MMRDA (Metro Line 6)** and **L&T (Metro Line 4)**. Two major metro wins (associated with L&T and IRCON) referenced as large-ticket. Public-project payment milestones keep the WC cycle clean.
- **Post-year-end:** new **Rs 100 cr order from IRCON** + an **Aligarh** order → order book **~Rs 2,000 cr+**.
- **Sports-complex pipeline ~Rs 244 cr** growth; positioned for 2030 Commonwealth/Olympic-linked sports-infra bids via Myrtha Pools.
- Key growth segments per mgmt: **Metro and sports**.

outlook.body:
- **Data centres — liquid-to-liquid cooling:** in process of tie-up with foreign tech companies; will inform shareholders before entering; no order-book commitment yet (update promised at Q2 call). Ties to the `Data-Center` theme.
- **Tunnel ventilation:** new segment; doing R&D, onboarding consultants, seeking tie-ups; first order ≥6 months away.
- **Aligarh land-monetization JV** (49%): real-estate/land-sale optionality — long-dated (see §8).
- **Sports/net-zero:** "perfectly timed" for Olympic/Commonwealth bid cycle and green-building demand.

deepdive.thesis: A small-cap Pune-based civil-infrastructure EPC contractor that inflected hard in FY26 — revenue +42% to Rs 243 cr, Q4 revenue +174% YoY to Rs 109 cr, PAT +65%+ to Rs 25.7 cr — riding a record Rs ~1,854 cr order book (~2x book-to-bill; ~Rs 2,000 cr+ after post-year-end wins). The pitch is a **Class 1A unlimited licence** (bids large government tenders solo, no JV margin-sharing) plus niche higher-margin verticals (Metro-BMS, tunnel ventilation, sports pools via Myrtha, data-centre cooling) where competition is lower. Management guides to Rs 600 cr (FY27) / Rs 900 cr (FY28) revenue with ~17–18% EBITDA and 10–11% PAT margins — a steep >2x scale-up that is largely execution- (not order-win-) dependent given Rs ~1,500 cr of backlog executable by FY28.
